Listen to this article Share In Nigeria’s competitive market for slimming products, the promise of a different body can be commercially powerful. But as concerns grow over product safety, effectiveness and marketing claims, ShapesLagos faces a defining test: whether a business built around body confidence can establish a lasting reputation grounded in evidence, transparency and responsible customer care. Founded by Lovelyn Okofu, ShapesLagos grew from her interest in fashion, body confidence and the challenges some women face in managing their weight, particularly after childbirth. What began as a desire to help women feel more comfortable in their bodies has developed into a wellness brand operating in an increasingly crowded weight-management market. Yet aspiration alone is not enough. Dramatic before-and-after photographs and customer testimonials can attract buyers, but individual experiences do not establish that a product caused a particular result or guarantee similar outcomes for others. For ShapesLagos, the opportunity is to turn its founding vision into a business that supports informed choices and responsibly communicates its products’ benefits and limitations. A brand rooted in body confidence Body image and weight management are deeply personal. Some women seek to manage changes after childbirth; others pursue broader health, fitness or personal goals. Diet, physical activity, sleep, underlying health conditions and individual metabolism can all influence outcomes. No single approach works identically for everyone. ShapesLagos offers WP Fat Blaster, Oolong Tea, Skinny Coffee, Dietary Fiber Protein Shake, Burn and Sum, and Flat Tummy Blaster. This range gives the company several product categories through which to engage consumers interested in weight management and nutritional support. It also makes accurate labelling, clear usage instructions and substantiated marketing essential. Customers need to know what each product contains, its intended purpose, how it should be used and what limitations may apply. Claims about weight loss or other health benefits should be supported by reliable evidence relevant to the finished product, rather than assumptions based solely on natural ingredients. Natural does not automatically mean safe. Ingredients can cause side effects, interact with medication or be unsuitable for people with particular medical conditions. Nor does a product’s advertised purpose establish its effectiveness. Consumers who are pregnant, breastfeeding, taking medication or managing an existing health condition should seek qualified medical advice where appropriate. Beyond testimonials Social media has become an important channel for wellness brands to build awareness and share customer experiences. But testimonials have clear limitations. Someone who reports losing weight after using a supplement may also have changed their diet, increased physical activity or adopted other lifestyle habits. Without appropriate evidence, it is difficult to establish how much of the result can be attributed to the product. Testimonials should therefore be presented as individual experiences, not universal promises or substitutes for scientific research. For ShapesLagos, credible communication means explaining the basis for advertised benefits, avoiding guarantees of rapid weight loss and disclosing material limitations. Any scientific or clinical evidence cited should be genuine, relevant to the specific product and available for appropriate scrutiny. The same standard applies to customer support. ShapesLagos places emphasis on guiding first-time users on how to use its products. Such guidance can help consumers understand labels, recommended directions and relevant precautions, but it should not be confused with medical supervision. Long-term customer care also requires accessible ingredient information, responsive complaint handling and a transparent process for reporting suspected adverse reactions. Taking complaints seriously and communicating honestly about their investigation can help establish a stronger basis for customer relationships than sales and positive reviews alone. Regulation and accountability Nigeria’s slimming and dietary supplement market operates in an environment where product safety, accurate labelling and regulatory compliance are essential. For ShapesLagos, continued growth should be accompanied by verifiable product information and compliance with applicable requirements of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), as well as relevant consumer-protection and advertising rules. Consumers should be able to verify applicable product registration details. Registration, where required and obtained, should not automatically be interpreted as proof that a product delivers every advertised weight-loss benefit. Similarly, claims that ingredients have been tested for safety or efficacy should be supported by documentation that accurately reflects the tests performed. If a brand describes its formulations as scientifically backed or developed with professional input, it should be able to substantiate those statements. These are standards for the industry as a whole, not allegations against any particular company. The information available for this article does not include independent product testing, regulatory records or clinical evidence sufficient to establish the safety or effectiveness of the ShapesLagos range. Its products should therefore not be described as clinically proven, guaranteed to produce weight loss or free from side effects without appropriate supporting evidence. For Okofu, accountability offers an opportunity to strengthen the brand’s credibility. Clear documentation, responsible advertising and a demonstrable commitment to consumer protection would give customers a more informed basis for their decisions. From founding vision to lasting reputation Okofu’s motivation provides a relatable starting point in a market where consumers invest not only money but also time and emotional energy in pursuit of personal goals. Yet a business’s long-term prospects depend on more than the intentions behind its creation. They require consistent standards, reliable product information and a willingness to place consumer welfare alongside commercial ambition. For ShapesLagos, the next chapter will depend on how effectively its founding vision translates into everyday business practices. The company must earn the confidence of customers who need clear information, realistic expectations and responsible guidance, rather than promises of rapid transformation. The strongest wellness brands will not necessarily be those promising the fastest results. They will be those that substantiate their claims, respect the people who use their products and recognise that customer wellbeing matters long after a sale has been completed. For ShapesLagos, that is the real test of growth: turning a commitment to body confidence into a business that earns trust through evidence, transparency and responsible service. Stephen Onyekwelu Stephen Onyekwelu is BusinessDay’s Strategy & Enterprise Delivery Executive, specialising in turning editorial vision into enterprise outcomes. A former Online News Editor and lead of the Go Local initiative (print, podcast & BDTV in partnership with Providus Bank), he blends investigative storytelling with platform strategy, conference design, and cross-functional delivery.
